clue.text: French statesman — one in Ibsen's work

indicators.note: the word in tells us the numeral one sits inside the title of the play

parts.note: Brand is an 1865 verse play by Henrik Ibsen
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A French politician has a part in a Norwegian drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Aristide Briand was a French prime minister several times over and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1926.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristide Briand was a leading politician of the Third Republic, eleven times premier of France.

clue.text: Carnivore familiar to London sight-seers ?

explanation.walkthrough: The Yeomen Warders at the Tower of London are known by this nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat-eater literally eats beef; the Tower of London's ceremonial guards, the Yeomen Warders, carry that nickname and are a tourist sight.

clue.text: Print journalist's announcement

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads as I'M PRESS, a reporter introducing themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress is to stamp or print a mark; a journalist announcing themselves might say 'I'm press'.

clue.text: For fresh gold, relies upon U.S. city

parts.note: fresh means new
or is the heraldic word for gold
leans means relies upon, as in leans on a friend

explanation.surface: Someone depends on an American city for a new gold supply.
explanation.definitionFit: New Orleans is the largest city in Louisiana, in the United States.

clue.text: Rites awe members, so to speak

indicators.note: the clue's letters are treated as members to be reassembled into a new group, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Religious ceremonies impress the people who belong, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' is an unusual signal: the letters of RITES AWE are the members, regrouped into a new phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms used to soften a figurative expression, meaning in a manner of talking.

clue.text: Glasses made for port, perhaps ?

explanation.walkthrough: 'made for port' means headed for harbour, not designed to hold wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooners are tall beer or sherry glasses, and also sailing vessels that might make for port.

clue.text: Mind a new florin?

explanation.walkthrough: The florin, two shillings, became ten new pence at decimalisation; read with 'd' for pence it is TEN D.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend is to look after; the florin was worth ten new pence after decimalisation, written here as ten d.

clue.text: No one has painful upset — all eating away!

indicators.note: upset in a down clue tells us the whole run of pieces is turned on its head

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
sore means painful

explanation.surface: Nobody feels hurt, yet everything is wearing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the whole run over, so the three pieces read bottom to top; 'has' and 'all' only join the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosion is the gradual wearing away of rock or soil, a gnawing destruction.

clue.text: Is abroad on work for bar

parts.note: est is the French for is
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A person is overseas working on a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' is the legal verb, to preclude, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to estop is to prevent a party from asserting something, to bar or preclude.

clue.text: Alternative mount in race as pace-maker

indicators.note: in tells us the reversed word sits inside the race abbreviation

parts.note: TT, the Tourist Trophy, is a motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: mount means rise, so in a down clue the word goes upwards

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A different horse in a race sets the pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' looks like a horse in a race, but it means climb, turning the alternative upward inside the Isle of Man race.
explanation.definitionFit: A trot is a gait or pace of a horse, the pace which a running speed is made at.

clue.text: Enable me to retire? Might !

indicators.note: to retire is to draw back, so the little word me goes backwards

parts.note: might means power or strength

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they may step down, then exclaims about strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retire' reads as stepping down from a job; it only turns the little word backwards before the synonym for might.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable someone is to give them the authority or means to act, a synonym.

clue.text: Striker makes statement to press ?

explanation.surface: A strike leader issues a press release.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hand' is a worker; one who is out on strike is a hand out, while the hyphenated word is a printed release.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker (a hand) who has come out on strike is literally a hand out; a press release given to journalists is a handout.

clue.text: It might excite Nora, curse it

indicators.note: it might be these letters in another order: the phrase points to a rearrangement of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A swear word, someone says, might get Nora worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It might' signals that EXCITE NORA, rearranged, makes the answer, a noun meaning a curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Execration is the act of cursing, or the curse uttered, a synonym of a noun sense.

clue.text: In all, I'm pretty flaccid

indicators.note: In tells us the answer lies inside the following run of words, across the word breaks

explanation.surface: Someone admits that, all things considered, they are rather droopy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points inside 'all, I'm pretty', where the letters run across the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp and flaccid are synonyms, both meaning soft and lacking firmness.

clue.text: It's a revelation !

parts.note: the phrase sounds like praise for a surprise, but names the last book of the Bible, also called Revelation

explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Revelation is also known by its Greek name meaning unveiling, a synonym.

clue.text: Sets new period for mosaic

indicators.note: new tells us the word sets is given a fresh arrangement of letters

parts.note: an era is a period of history

explanation.surface: Someone establishes a fresh age, presumably in art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns SETS into TESS, followed by ERA. The definition is loose: a tessera is one small tile of a mosaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is a small cube of stone or glass set into a mosaic pavement, a part standing for the whole.

clue.text: Painful thing about naval error -means danger in high places

indicators.note: about tells us the painful thing goes around the jumbled letters

parts.note: an ache is a painful thing

indicators.note: error tells us the letters of naval are wrongly ordered

explanation.surface: Something hurtful about a naval mistake signals peril up high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' signals that the word naval is jumbled, and the result sits inside the ache after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An avalanche is a mass of snow sliding down a mountain, a peril of the heights.

clue.text: Stretch of river holds vessels

indicators.note: holds tells us the river's name wraps round the vessels

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword favourite
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: A section of a river contains boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessels' suggests ships in a river; here they are cooking pans.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse is a wide stretch of land, water or sky, a synonym.

clue.text: A simple job, the professor's-- comfortable too

definitions.note: describes the seat: a chair that is also comfortable

parts.note: easy means simple
a chair is a professor's post

explanation.surface: A straightforward post, a professorship, and a cosy one besides.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes rather than names: a chair that is comfortable as well.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy chair is a large upholstered armchair, a seat made for comfort.

clue.text: Girls meet right back in Italy

indicators.note: back tells us the run of names and letter is read backwards as a whole

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
Eva is another girl's name

explanation.surface: Young women meet up again in an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girls' supplies two names, and 'back' reverses the names and the R together. 'in Italy' defines by location.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenna is a city in northern Italy, famous for its Byzantine mosaics, so it is a place found within that country.

clue.text: Their eyes are on central Latvia

definitions.text: Their eyes are on central Latvia

parts.words: Their eyes are on central Latvia
parts.note: the middle of Latvia is the letters TV, so this describes people watching the television

explanation.definitionFit: Television audiences are people who watch a screen, their eyes on the TV.

clue.text: Sees about the mangy brute-ties him up

definitions.note: a verb phrase with its object: secures him

indicators.note: about tells us the first word goes around the description of the animal

parts.note: a cur is a mangy mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone notices a scruffy dog and tethers it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sees' is used as its own letters, not as a verb; the definition carries its object 'him' with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure someone is to fasten or tie them firmly, so the verb fits tying him up.

clue.text: Ignores trouble in the districts

indicators.note: trouble tells us the letters of ignores are disturbed

explanation.surface: Someone disregards unrest in the provinces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges IGNORES.
explanation.definitionFit: Regions and districts are synonyms for areas of a country.

clue.text: Grounds are meadows, say?

indicators.note: say tells us the word for meadows is spoken and a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: leas are meadows or grassland

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a sports ground is really just fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds' means sediment, as in coffee grounds, not sports fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Lees are the sediment at the bottom of wine, like coffee grounds, the dregs.

clue.text: Animal rears a beetle !

indicators.note: rears means lifts up, so in a down clue the run is read from the bottom

parts.note: a beetle is a heavy wooden mallet, also called a mall or maul

explanation.surface: A creature rears up at an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beetle' is the heavy mallet, not the insect; A + MALL reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A llama is a South American animal of the camel family.

clue.text: A way none reason concerning diseases

parts.note: a path is a way
nought, the letter O, means none
logic is reason

explanation.surface: An argument by a route no rational mind would take about illnesses.
explanation.walkthrough: Using 'none' for the letter O, a zero, is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathologic is an old form of pathological, relating to the study of diseases.

clue.text: He has a large number of pupils

definitions.text: He has a large number of pupils

parts.words: He has a large number of pupils
parts.note: sounds like someone with many eyes

explanation.definitionFit: The head is the principal of a school, responsible for all its students.

clue.text: Catch duck up in Scotland

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the run is read from the bottom

parts.note: nab means catch
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone bags a duck while shooting in the Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a seaside town in western Scotland, a place located there.

clue.text: Blame repairer in charge of the old vessel

indicators.note: a repairer puts things back together, so the letters of blame are refitted in a new order

explanation.surface: Blame the mechanic who was in charge of the antique pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repairer' looks like a person but signals that the letters of the first word are refitted in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: An alembic was an early distilling apparatus used by alchemists, a vessel of former times.

clue.text: A speed-scale or a jar

parts.note: mph, miles per hour, is a scale for measuring speed

explanation.surface: A choice between a speedometer and a jar.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a two-handled ancient Greek or Roman storage jar.

clue.text: Animal came in with no hesitation, it's agreed

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: with no tells us the sound of hesitation is taken out of the verb before

parts.note: entered means came in
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A creature walked in without pausing, and everyone concurred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' takes the hesitation sound out of the synonym for came in, before the animal's letters are joined on.
explanation.definitionFit: To assent is to agree, so assented is the past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Twisted muscle gets no rest

indicators.note: twisted tells us the letters of no rest are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: A pulled muscle denies someone any peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted muscle' reads as an injury; 'muscle' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tensor is a muscle that tightens or stretches a part of the body.
